Best Restaurants in Jersey for Every Budget

November 19, 2026
By: Steph Parker
18
Nov
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 12:49
Instaread

Looking for the best restaurants in Jersey, Channel Islands?

From beach cafés and harbour-side snacks, to Michelin-starred tasting menus, these independent and characterful places make it easy to eat well, whatever your budget.

Jersey may be small, but it has a food scene with plenty of personality – from crab sandwiches on harbour walls and relaxed lunches with sea views all the way through to fine dining-starred dinners.

And its position in the Channel brings a lovely mix of British comfort food, French influences and excellent local seafood.

This guide covers restaurants in Jersey for every budget, with options across the capital St Helier, as well as the island’s best bays and villages…

  • How to Visit Jersey on a Budget

Restaurants in Jersey at a Glance

Budget Typical spend per person Good for
Cheap eats    About £5-£18 Cafés, kiosks, brunch and beach snacks
Mid-range About £18-£40 Independent bistros, pub dining and relaxed seafood  
Luxury About £50+ Tasting menus, special occasions and fine dining

These are useful planning bands rather than strict price limits. A drink, starter, dessert or seafood special can quickly nudge up the bill.

Prices are indicative per person for a main meal, and menus can change with the season.

Check the restaurant’s website before booking.

 

Cheap Eats in Jersey

The Ugly Oyster Seafood Bar, Grève de Lecq

For oysters and local seafood at the beach, try this seasonal seafood bar at Grève de Lecq.

It serves freshly shucked oysters, lobster rolls and sustainably sourced seafood in a relaxed street-food setting, making it a fun stop after a north coast walk.

It is not a full-service restaurant, and prices depend on what you order, so think of it as a casual seafood treat.

It usually opens seasonally, so do check their social media pages before setting off.

The Hungry Man, Rozel Bay

A Jersey classic, The Hungry Man is a tiny, colourful café perched on Rozel Harbour.

It’s known for generous burgers, crab sandwiches, homemade cakes, as well as its famously over-the-top marshmallow hot chocolate and “double decker health wrecker” sandwich.

The location is half the fun – grab a seat overlooking the harbour and watch the little fishing boats bob about while you eat.

Come for a relaxed lunch full of local character – sunny days get busy, so do Sundays.

Opening hours are seasonal.

Mad Mary’s Beach Café, Bouley Bay

For quirky seaside snacks, Mad Mary’s is hard to beat.

The café sits above Bouley Bay, with views over the water and a personality all its own.

It is particularly famous for Bouley burgers and hot chocolate, making it a welcome reward after braving the bay’s waters.

Check current opening information before setting off, as this small beach café is seasonal.

The winding approach is part of the adventure FYI!

The Good Egg Beach Café, Havre des Pas

Just outside St Helier, this friendly independent café serves all-day brunch, pancakes and lighter dishes beside the sea.

It’s a good choice if you want a proper sit-down breakfast or lunch without committing to a full evening restaurant bill.

There are vegan and vegetarian options too, plus children’s choices and dog-friendly touches too.

Its beach-clean-for-coffee exchange lets you help collect litter on the shore before enjoying a coffee.

Lifeboat Café, Albert Pier

For a practical, no-fuss meal in St Helier, head to the Lifeboat Café on Albert Pier.

This harbour café serves breakfast rolls, coffee, fish specials, chips, burgers and Jersey ice cream, with outdoor seating and views across the harbour.

It’s especially handy if you’re catching a boat, exploring the waterfront, or simply want a quick bite among the local maritime bustle.

Bonne Nuit Beach Café, Bonne Nuit Bay

Thai food, harbour views and BYO wine? That’s a budget-friendly combination I can get behind!

This relaxed café beside Bonne Nuit Bay serves classic Thai dishes alongside local seafood, with takeaway available too.

Its BYO policy helps keep the drinks bill down, making it a lovely choice for an affordable evening meal on Jersey’s north coast.

Bring your favourite bottle and check any corkage charges when booking.

 

Mid Range Restaurants in Jersey

The Lookout Beach Café, St Helier

The Lookout is a great choice when you want a proper restaurant meal with a beach view, but don’t want to go full fine dining.

It sits at First Tower, a short walk from St Helier, overlooking St Aubin’s Bay and Elizabeth Castle.

The menu includes seafood, salads, burgers and beachside classics, with vegan and vegetarian choices.

Current menu examples include a classic burger at £17 and fish and chips at £20, so this is at the upper edge of a mid-range meal.

Go for lunch or an early dinner and you get the views without needing to book a special occasion.

The Lookout is open year-round, with raclette and fondue appearing in the winter.

Le Braye Café, St Ouen’s Bay

Family-run Le Braye is a relaxed beachside bistro with a menu inspired by British seaside classics and Mediterranean flavours.

Its location beside St Ouen’s Bay makes it an easy choice after a beach day or coastal walk, with breakfast, brunch, lunch and dinner options.

Expect a more substantial bill than at a kiosk, but a lovely setting for a leisurely meal.

Check its website or social channels for current menus and opening hours.

Fun fact, I used to work here!

The Cock & Bottle, St Helier

This atmospheric town pub retains original features and serves French dishes alongside Jersey pub favourites.

It’s location in the Royal Square is hard to beat, especially in the summer months.

Pair dinner with local Mary Ann Best Bitter or Liberation Ale.

CaféJac at Jersey Arts Centre

CaféJac is a relaxed café for breakfast, coffee or casual dinner, with fresh juices and a broad menu.

Its central Arts Centre location is handy before a show or on a rainy afternoon in the heart of St Helier.

Oyster Box, St Brelade’s Bay

For seafood with a view, Oyster Box sits right beside the sand at St Brelade’s Bay, serving Jersey rock oysters, fresh fish and other local produce.

It feels like a special occasion restaurant, but its Market Menu offers good value – £22.50 for two courses or £27.50 for three.

It’s available Tuesday to Saturday for lunch and dinner, plus Sunday lunch.

Book ahead for a sea-view table.

Beresford House, Formerly Banjo, St Helier

If you remember Banjo, the historic restaurant at 8 Beresford Street has reopened as Beresford House, with The Dining Room and Conservatory offering all-day dining.

Its set menu is a good-value way to enjoy the grand Victorian surroundings – currently £26.50 for two courses or £32.50 for three, Monday to Saturday.

Menus include brasserie favourites and Jersey produce.

Check the current menu and booking details before you go.

 

Top Restaurants in Jersey

Bohemia, St Helier

For a big-ticket meal, Bohemia is Jersey’s Michelin-starred standout, retaining its star for 2026 as the island’s only starred restaurant.

Expect ambitious cooking with local ingredients, plus tasting, vegetarian tasting and à la carte menus.

The restaurant is inside The Club Hotel & Spa in St Helier.

Book well in advance for weekend dinners, and check the current menu and price when reserving, as the experience and seasonal dishes change.

For a special treat, the Chef’s Table offers a view over the kitchen pass.

Ocean Restaurant, St Ouen’s Bay

Ocean Restaurant at The Atlantic Hotel pairs fine dining with a dramatic setting above St Ouen’s Bay.

Its seasonal menu showcases Jersey produce and seafood.

Current menu examples include Jersey oysters at £12 for 3, Jersey Royal velouté at £14, and mains such as sea bream at £27 or dry-aged bavette at £36.

A discretionary 10% service charge is added.

For a more budget-conscious taste of the setting, the lunch menu is served Monday to Saturday.

Pêtchi, St Helier

Pêtchi is a stylish splurge for food lovers, with a wood-fired open kitchen, Jersey ingredients and Basque-inspired cooking.

The menu might include whole fish, ex-dairy beef chops, Jersey oysters and crab, with small plates and dishes designed for sharing.

It is listed in the Michelin Guide and overlooks Liberation Square in St Helier.

Check its current à la carte and set-lunch menus before booking – opening days vary across the week.

Samphire, St Helier

For a polished but relaxed meal, try Samphire on Don Street.

Its seasonal, locally sourced menu features Jersey oysters, hand-dived scallops, seafood, meat and creative vegetable dishes.

The weekday Regional Table set menu is currently £38 for two courses or £45 for three, available Tuesday to Friday at lunch and dinner.

That makes it one of the clearest ways to plan a special meal without going straight to a luxury tasting menu.

Book ahead, especially for Saturday dining.

 

How to Eat Well in Jersey for Less

  • Make lunch your main restaurant meal. Several of the island’s smarter restaurants offer set menus or lighter lunch options.
  • Choose beach cafés for memorable views without paying for a formal dining room.
  • Look for seasonal dishes, especially Jersey Royals, oysters, scallops and local crab.
  • Check whether a menu is à la carte or set-price before you book, and remember to allow for drinks and any service charge.
  • Plan transport before dinner. St Helier is walkable, and easier to reach by bus, than many coastal restaurants.
  • Book ahead for popular beachside spots in summer and for fine dining throughout the year.

 

Frequently Asked Questions about Restaurants in Jersey

What Is the Best Restaurant in Jersey?

For Michelin-starred fine dining, Bohemia is the island’s standout.

For a memorable beach café, try The Hungry Man in Rozel or Mad Mary’s at Bouley Bay.

The best choice depends on your budget and the sort of atmosphere you want.

Are Restaurants in Jersey Expensive?

They can be, particularly for seafood and fine dining, but there are plenty of cafés, kiosks and casual places where you can eat for around £5-£18 per person.

A set lunch menu is often a good-value way to try a higher-end restaurant.

Where Can I Eat Jersey Seafood?

Look for Jersey oysters, crab, scallops and locally caught fish at restaurants such as Samphire, Ocean Restaurant, The Lookout and seaside cafés around the island.

Availability depends on season and daily supply.

Do I Need to Book Restaurants in Jersey?

Book fine dining restaurants ahead, plus popular coastal spots in summer.

Cafés are more flexible, though sunny days can bring queues.

Is Jersey the Same as New Jersey?

No.

This guide is about Jersey in the Channel Islands, a British Crown Dependency in the English Channel, not the US state of New Jersey!

 

Mini Travel Guide to Jersey

Getting There

Flying from the UK can be done cheaply, with easyJet, Jet2 and British Airways all flying to Jersey.

Check out Skyscanner for some great deals.

Otherwise, catch the ferry from Poole, Portsmouth, St Malo in France or Guernsey.

Learn more about how to travel to Jersey from London in this complete guide I wrote.

When to Visit

May through September are the best months to visit the island in my opinion.

How Long to Spend There

3-7 days is a great amount of time to get a feel for all Jersey has to offer.

Getting Around Jersey

Walking is free and easy across this small island, or there is a good local bus service – Liberty Bus – which has a very cost-effective set of Hop-On Hop-Off passes, perfect for visitors.

You can also rent bikes.

Sadly Uber hasn’t reached Jersey yet, so you’d be better to hire a car if you’re looking for some independence when it comes to transport.
